title: FORTA: Byzantine-Resilient FL Aggregation via DFT-Guided Krum

C-a.quote: These steps, repeated until convergence of the global model, consist of: secret sharing of local updates over infinite fields, outlier detection with feedback from the DFT decoder, and secure aggregation of selected users followed by a global model update.
C-a.locator: Sec. III / Fig. 1; the paper's own decomposition puts DETECTION IN ONE STEP, and only that step carries a poisoning-resistance purpose. The step is a single mechanism: "we employ an outlier detection mechanism based on pairwise distances between model updates, specifically leveraging the Krum aggregation rule [4]" (Sec. II). AMENDMENT 3 EXCLUDES THE OTHER TWO STEPS: the secret sharing and the secure aggregation are privacy-purposed -- "enabling privacy-preserving pairwise distance computation without quantization" (Sec. I) -- and their inclusion is justified against gradient inversion, "adversaries can exploit gradient inversion techniques to reconstruct private training datasets" (Sec. I). THE GMM STAGE IS THE CLOSE CALL AND IT IS DISCUSSED IN THE NOTE: "We propose a joint decoding strategy based on Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) that improves adversarial localization by distinguishing structured attacks from precision noise in the DFT decoder" (Sec. I). It is coded as machinery of the decoder rather than a second mechanism, because its output is the input to the one detection rule -- "The frequency profile yields a vector f where fi denotes how often user i is flagged as adversarial" (Sec. III), consumed by "a modified Krum rule that integrates frequency-based feedback from the DFT decoder" (Sec. I)

C-b.quote: However, such an approach can suffer from numerical errors and overflows when applied to real-valued model updates, motivating the need for secure aggregation methods that operate directly over the real domain.
C-b.locator: Sec. I; every stated reason in the paper concerns PRECISION AND PRIVACY, not the pairing of two defenses. The three design goals are listed as "(i) preserve privacy, (ii) ensure robustness against adversarial updates, and (iii) remain effective under finite precision constraints" (Sec. II), which is a requirements list rather than a complementarity argument, and the deficiency that motivates the GMM stage is numerical, "finite precision introduces numerical perturbations that can distort distance estimates and allow malicious updates to evade detection" (Sec. I). No quotation gives a reason for pairing two defense mechanisms on their constituent properties

C-c.quote: Fig. 2: Test accuracy over training rounds on i.i.d. MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets, comparing FedAvg, Krum, and Modified Krum under Byzantine attacks.
C-c.locator: Sec. IV; the metric is the assembled framework's own test accuracy under Byzantine attack across training rounds, and the summary claim is "experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 demonstrated that FORTA significantly outperforms standard Krum and FedAvg under Byzantine threats" (Sec. V)

C-d.quote: Original Krum offers better performance than FedAvg but suffers in test accuracy when compared to modified Krum, validating the benefits of DFT-guided Krum.
C-d.locator: Sec. IV; CODED YES UNDER RULE 4. The Krum-against-Modified-Krum arm plausibly holds the downstream selection rule fixed while varying the signal that reaches it: the feedback enters as soft confidences, "We convert this into soft confidences" via a softmax over the frequency profile (Sec. III), so uniform confidences recover standard Krum and the arm isolates the decoder-derived signal. Only ONE thing changes between the two arms, which distinguishes it from ArKrum's rKrum-against-ArKrum comparison, where two enhancements move together. THE STRICT READING IS RECORDED: the paper calls the result "a modified Krum rule" (Sec. I), i.e. a change to the rule rather than to its input, and on that reading C-d = NO. The code does not affect this row's primary either way, since C-a = NO

C-e.quote: This enhances the selection of reliable users, significantly improving robustness under precision-aware Byzantine attacks.
C-e.locator: Sec. I, contribution 4; the claim names the constituent (the DFT-guided feedback) and states what it contributes to the composed result. The same attribution is restated as a measured finding at Sec. IV in the C-d quotation, and the framework-level version is at Sec. V, "we integrated decoder-derived feedback into a modified Krum aggregator, dynamically reweighting user contributions based on estimated adversarial likelihood"

coder_note:
C-a = NO EXTENDS A CONSISTENCY CHAIN THAT NOW HAS FOUR MEMBERS, AND THAT CHAIN IS THE REASON FOR THE CODE RATHER THAN ANYTHING SPECIAL ABOUT THIS PAPER. refined-Krum (2311.15894), MASA (2411.01040), ArKrum (2505.17226) and FORTA all compose a preparatory computation with a single Krum-derived or unlearning-derived selection rule, where the preparatory stage exists to repair a quantity the rule needs -- an adversary count, a fused representation, an f-estimate, a distance estimate corrupted by finite precision. Every one is coded C-a = NO on the ground that machinery feeding one mechanism's internal quantity is that mechanism in stages. If a reader rejects that reading, all four rows move together, which is the property I wanted: the call is a rubric-level policy, not four separate judgments.

THE COUNTER-READING FOR THIS PAPER IS THE STRONGEST IN THE CHAIN AND IS RECORDED SO IT CAN BE OVERTURNED. The GMM joint-decoding stage is not merely arithmetic repair: it performs its own statistical discrimination, "isolates adversarial indices by statistically separating them from noiseaffected but honest evaluations" (Sec. III), and emits a per-user adversarial frequency profile. A reader could reasonably call that a detector, in which case FORTA composes two detectors -- code-domain error localization and distance-based selection -- and C-a = YES. Two things kept me at NO: the paper's own three-step decomposition places detection in a single step, and rule 3 requires the reading that does not make the paper outcome-gated where a quotation supports two. With C-b = NO independently, the DESIGN code is unaffected by this call.

THE PRIVACY SUBSTRATE HERE IS LOAD-BEARING FOR THE DEFENSE, WHICH IS A CONFIGURATION AMENDMENT 3 DOES NOT ANTICIPATE. In DDFed the privacy stage sat beside the defenses and could be excised from the count cleanly. In FORTA the DFT code IS how the pairwise distances get computed at all, so the privacy mechanism is not a neighbour of the detector but its substrate, and the finite-precision noise it introduces is what creates the attack the paper then defends against ("Byzantine users craft perturbations that closely mimic finite-precision noise", Sec. I). Amendment 3 still gives the right answer -- the substrate's stated purpose is privacy, so it does not count toward two -- but A5 should note this as a third configuration of the privacy class, after DDFed's separable stages and ArKrum's title-only privacy.
